# Monstera repotting

## Montgomery

The Monstera deliciosa, known in this house as Montgomery, came from the plant stall at Newton Abbot market in 2021 for £9 in a 12 cm pot. By spring 2025 it had eleven leaves, the biggest 58 cm across, and roots coming out of the drainage holes of a 24 cm pot like grey spaghetti. It had to happen.

It also had to come out of the hallway anyway while Colin and I did the walls, see [[Painting the hallway]], so I killed two birds.

## The mix

Chunky aroid mix, made up on the kitchen table on newspaper:

- 3 parts orchid bark (medium grade, Westland, £6.49 for 8 L)
- 2 parts coir
- 1 part perlite
- 1 part worm castings from Alfie's wormery
- a handful of horticultural charcoal

Nothing straight from the bag of multipurpose. Last time I used that, in 2023, it stayed soggy at the bottom for weeks and I got gnats (see [[Fungus gnats]]).

## On the day, 12 April 2025

- Watered the day before so the root ball slid out
- Teased the circling roots loose, cut off three dead ones, brown and hollow
- New pot 30 cm, terracotta, £21 from Moorland Garden Centre
- Moss pole 90 cm, coir-wrapped, tied in the two aerial roots with soft twine
- Left it in the bathroom in bright shade for a week to get over it

Took 1 hour 40 minutes including clearing up. The pot with soil and plant weighs 14.6 kg on the bathroom scales, which I now regret.

## Afterwards

Sulked for two weeks, one lower leaf yellowed and came off. New leaf unfurled 19 May with three proper splits. Watering only when the top 5 cm are dry, every 9 to 12 days in summer, as logged in [[Watering schedule]].
